title: Zero derived integral reduction makes multiplication by ℓ invertible
statement: For prime ℓ, a normed ℚ_ℓ-algebra field E, any scheme X and any unbounded complex K of internal O_E coefficient modules, with coefficients and reduction as in [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], if the derived reduction of K modulo ℓ is zero, multiplication by ℓ on K is an isomorphism. No finite dimensionality, constructibility, boundedness or noetherianity is assumed.

source.place: Section 6.5, the two-term residue resolution and derived tensor

proof.text: The already proved coefficient sequence O_E --ℓ--> O_E --> O_E/(ℓ) is short exact. Exact inverse image takes it to X. Faithful exact forgetting of the internal module structure reflects short exactness, giving a free two-term resolution of the restricted residue module.

Choose a K-flat representative P of K. The counit comparison for left derived extension of scalars is an isomorphism on P. Zero derived reduction therefore makes its ordinary scalar extension acyclic. The extension/forgetting tensor comparison, and then the braiding, imply that P tensor the restricted residue module is acyclic.

Apply the proved source-library DerivedCategory.reductionIso to the coefficient short exact sequence and P. It identifies the derived residue tensor with the cone of ℓ times the identity of P. That cone is zero, hence the first morphism of its distinguished triangle is invertible. Transport along the chosen representative isomorphism yields invertibility of ℓ times the identity of K.

proof_origin.note: Fully proved. A generic categorical auxiliary avoids unfolding the large concrete coefficient definitions repeatedly; the same module now compiles well below 60 seconds.
